subject: Emotions
title: Humor and Incongruity
description: A quick, practical guide to Humor and Incongruity.

hook.text: Why did the chicken cross the road? You groan because you expected surprise and got none. Humor needs the unexpected.

buildup.text: The incongruity theory says humor arises when reality violates a pattern in a safe, non-threatening way.

discovery.text: Brain scans of people hearing jokes show the same surprise circuits firing before the laughter begins.

twist.text: Puns are the lowest form of surprise—a minor expectation violation. Absurdist humor is the highest.

climax.text: Children laugh 300 times a day; adults laugh 20. We lose humor because we lose the capacity for surprise.

punchline.text: Every joke is a tiny ambush your brain forgives.

quiz.question: What theory explains humor through violated expectations?
